bib.title: INCODER: A GENERATIVE MODEL FOR CODE INFILLING AND SYNTHESIS

read.skipped: Appendix D qualitative example figures are garbled token soup and were only skimmed; references skimmed.

question: Can one generative code model trained with a causal masking objective do both left-to-right program synthesis and zero-shot infilling of arbitrary code spans using bidirectional context?
hypothesis: Conditioning on right context via causal-masked infilling improves zero-shot editing tasks without hurting left-to-right synthesis.
contributions: INCODER, the first large generative code model able to infill arbitrary regions of code
Zero-shot infilling benchmarks (HumanEval single/multi-line, type hints, variable names, docstrings)
Ablations showing causal masking does not hurt left-to-right synthesis and StackOverflow data helps
Public release of models and code

method.summary: A 6.7B decoder-only Transformer trained for one epoch on 159 GB code (28 languages) plus 57 GB StackOverflow with a causal masking objective: spans are replaced by sentinels and moved to the end of the document. At inference the same model does left-to-right generation or infilling, compared with left-to-right single and left-to-right reranking baselines on the same weights.
method.task: causal-masked language modelling of code; zero-shot code infilling and synthesis

datasets.name: GitHub/GitLab permissive code
datasets.size: 159 GB of code (52 GB Python); about 670,000 repos; 28 languages
datasets.split: one epoch, each document used once
datasets.source: public non-fork repos with MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD-2 or BSD-3 licence, collected through Dec 9 2021, plus Python/Jupyter from GitHub archive on BigQuery
datasets.preprocessing: Exact-match dedup on alphanumeric token sequence (removed ~75% by size, 1 TB to 250 GB); emails replaced by removed@example.com; filtered files with line >3000 tokens, mean line >100 tokens, <40% alphanumeric/underscore, or auto-generated; decontamination vs CodeSearchNet val/test and JuICe eval repos; decontamination plus filtering remove ~10% of Python files; metadata (filename, extension, source, binned stars) inserted at start with p=50% else at end; Jupyter cells in XML-style tags

datasets.name: StackOverflow
datasets.source: questions with at least one answer, up to ten non-negative-score answers per question, up to five comments per question/answer
datasets.preprocessing: tags and binned votes as metadata

datasets.name: HumanEval infilling (single and multi-line)
datasets.size: single-line: one example per non-blank line; multi-line: N(N+1)/2 per function of N lines

datasets.name: CodeXGLUE return type hints
datasets.preprocessing: AST filter to non-None return hints; other hints stripped

datasets.name: TypeWriter OSS
datasets.preprocessing: only files not in training data

models.name: INCODER-6.7B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer, dense 6.7B config of Artetxe et al. 2021
models.tokenizer: byte-level BPE trained on corpus; tokens may span whitespace (not newlines); 45% fewer tokens than GPT-2 BPE

other.note: ablation models; 2.3B LM also trained, config not given

training.objective: causal masking: sample span count from Poisson mean 1 truncated to [1,256] (single span ~50% of the time); span endpoints uniform, resample on overlap; maximise log P([Left; <Mask:0>; Right; <Mask:0>; Span; <EOM>]); cross-entropy on all tokens except mask sentinels
training.optimizer: Adam, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98, gradient norm clip 1.0

other.framework: Fairseq, PyTorch, FairScale fully sharded model states

inference.decoding: top-p nucleus sampling p=0.95 with task-tuned temperature (greedy for some tasks)
inference.temperature: HumanEval infill: 0.2 for L-R single and CM, 0.8 for reranking; docstring: greedy for CM and L-R single, 0.8 for reranking; type hints: 0.2 L-R single, 0.8 reranking, greedy CM; HumanEval synthesis: 0.2 for pass@1, 0.8 for pass@10/100
inference.max_tokens: task-specific stop criteria (<EOM>, newline, ':' for types); window 2048
inference.samples: Reranking: K=10 candidates (25 for variable names). HumanEval synthesis: 200 samples per problem, unbiased estimator. MBPP pass@1: single candidate.
inference.prompting: zero-shot; prompts prefixed with metadata marking Python; infill inserts <Mask:0> and appends an extra <Mask:1> sentinel to avoid infill length bias; Codex templated prompt

parameters.rerank scoring: total or mean log prob chosen per task on dev set
parameters.variable names: only names with 4 or more characters; most common prediction across masks

metrics.name: pass rate
metrics.definition: completed function passes all input-output pairs (pass@1 analogue)

metrics.name: type accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match on normalised (AST parse/unparse) type hint

eval.protocol: Temperatures tuned on dev data per task and method; 95% CIs by bootstrap in Fig 2; no seeds reported.

availability.data: training corpus not released; evaluation benchmarks built from public datasets

prompts.text:
[code before the infill mask] <INFILL> [code after the infill mask]
# Complete the above code by replacing the <INFILL> tag.
[code before the infill mask]

limits: Validation perplexity still falling after one epoch (Fig 4); model undertrained.
Cross-paper comparisons in Table 11 are not rigorous (architecture, data, procedure differ).
Left-to-right Codex and CodeGen-Mono beat INCODER on HumanEval.
code-davinci-002 infills far better (87.4 vs 69.0) and its training is undisclosed.
Type hint exact match is noisy; TypeWriter eval is a filtered subset.
No learning rate, weight decay, or precision stated.
Cloze task: Codex may have seen CodeSearchNet.
